Metadata.title: The Library of Babel
Metadata.description: A library that holds every possible book — every combination of characters that can ever be written.

Footer.credit: Inspired by Jorge Luis Borges’ short story “The Library of Babel” (1941)

hero.epigraph: The Library holds every possible book — every combination of characters that can ever be written.

search.title: Search the Library
search.text: Type any text, and the Library will point to the exact page it is written on, somewhere among its endless volumes.

quotes.universe: The universe — some call it the Library — is made up of a vast, perhaps endless number of hexagonal galleries.
quotes.shelves: Every wall of every hexagon carries five shelves; every shelf, thirty-two volumes, all of the same size.
quotes.eternity: The Library has existed ab aeterno. No sound mind can doubt this truth, and from it follows at once that the world will last forever.
quotes.everything: Everything is there: a history of the future down to the last detail, the autobiographies of archangels, the true catalogue of the Library, and thousands upon thousands of false ones...

structure.title: How the Library is built
structure.galleryText: Every gallery has six walls. Five of them are lined with shelves; the sixth opens onto a vestibule with a mirror, a spiral staircase and the next gallery.
structure.wallsText: Every wall has seven shelves, and every shelf holds thirty-one volumes of the same size.
structure.pagesText: Every volume has four hundred and twenty-one pages, each of them four thousand eight hundred and nineteen characters long.
structure.booksText: The Library holds every possible combination of {symbols, plural, one {# symbol} other {# symbols}}: letters of both cases, digits, the space, the line break and punctuation marks. Every conceivable book has already been written.

explore.title: Explore the Library
explore.searchText: Find any text ever written, or not yet written. Every thought is already recorded on one of the pages.
explore.browseText: Pick a wall, a shelf, a volume and a page. Move through the Library like one of Borges’ librarians.
explore.galleryText: Step into a hexagonal gallery and look over its shelves in three dimensions. Feel the scale of infinity.

how.title: How it works
how.addressText: Every page has a unique address: a long string of digits and Latin letters, followed by its wall, shelf, volume and page.
how.determinismText: A page’s content is fully defined by its address. The same address always leads to the same text.
how.reversibilityText: Any text can be found: the algorithm computes the exact address where the text you typed is written.
how.completenessText: Every possible combination of symbols exists. You do not create a text; you find it in the endless Library.

finalQuote.text: “The Library is limitless and periodic. An eternal wanderer setting out in any direction would find, after centuries, that the same books recur in the same disorder — a disorder which, recurring, becomes an order: the Order.”

Browse.title: Browse the Library
Browse.text: Pick a place in the Library — a wall, a shelf, a volume and a page — and open a random book.

Gallery.bannerUp: You have climbed to the gallery one floor up. The staircase goes on upwards.
Gallery.bannerDown: You have gone down to the gallery one floor below. The staircase goes on downwards.
Gallery.bannerNext: You have entered the next gallery. The same shelves, different books.
Gallery.hintDesktop: W A S D — walk, Shift — run, space — jump, wheel — zoom. Click a volume or a shelf. The spiral staircase in the vestibule leads to the galleries above and below; the far door leads to the next one.
Gallery.hintTouch: Drag a finger to look around; use two fingers to walk. Tap a volume or a shelf.
Gallery.lockOn: The mouse steers your gaze · a click opens what is under the crosshair · Esc releases the cursor
Gallery.lockOff: Click the scene to steer with the mouse, like in a game · Esc releases the cursor

Shelf.tooltipGo: Wall {wall} · Shelf {shelf} — go to this shelf
Shelf.hint: The lit shelf is the open one: it holds {volumes, plural, one {# volume} other {# volumes}}. Hover over a spine to read its title, click to open the volume.
Shelf.hintDesktop: The mouse wheel zooms; clicking another shelf takes you there.

Volume.hint: The volume has {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}}. Point at a number in the index and click to open that page.
Volume.hintDesktop: Drag with the mouse to tilt the book; the wheel zooms.

Reader.notFoundTitle: There is no such address in the Library
Reader.notFoundText: A page address looks like this: the gallery’s characters, then the wall, shelf, volume and page, separated by hyphens.
Reader.hint: Click the right page or press → to turn it; click the left page or press ← to go back. Turn quickly and the pages fan out.
Reader.hintDesktop: Drag or WASD to move over the book, the wheel flies to the spot under the cursor, ↑ ↓ bring it closer or farther, right-drag tilts, Home shows the whole book. L or a click of the wheel takes a loupe: the wheel changes its magnification, Esc puts it away.
Reader.loupeTitle: Loupe (L or a click of the mouse wheel): move it over the book, the wheel changes the magnification, Esc puts it away
